annotations.text:
A · Sketch grid — the attached sketch, literally.
Two by two at every width, screenshots tilted and broken out of the card top. Reads as a toy shelf.
Tradeoff: at 390px the two-up cards leave ~150px of text width, so the blurbs have to be short — that is the least SEO copy of the three.

B · Marquee row — four abreast, editorial hero.
Left-aligned hero so the h1 and the paragraph read as one block; cards straight-on and equal weight.
Tradeoff: four equal cards say all four tools are equally real. Three of them are not.

C · Featured — the shipped tool leads.
The dex builder gets a split hero card with a real screenshot and a solid CTA; the other three sit in a supporting row.
Tradeoff: it buries the league builder, which is the tool with a settled spec and the next page to rank.

SEO structure, same in all three:
· h1 carries "make your own Pokédex" plus region and league.
· Each card is an <h2> that exactly matches its slug: /custom-pokedex-builder, /pokemon-league-builder, /favorite-pokemon-picker.
· The footer repeats the four links as anchor text.
Watch out: making / a router moves the dex builder off the URL that ranks today (~pos 7.8 for "pokedex builder").

D · Poster cards — the artwork is anchored to the card's BOTTOM edge, where it is clipped flush, and runs up past the TOP edge. Every frame here is a real device viewport, so nothing scrolls: 390×844, 834×1112, 1440×900.
The two mobile frames are the same layout with two ways of keeping the copy readable. Pick one.

Gradient. The screenshot reaches the card's bottom edge and a white scrim rises over its lower third; the h2 and the line under it sit on the scrim.
More screenshot stays visible, and the card reads as one object rather than a picture with a caption.
Cost: the copy sits on a busy sprite grid, so it needs the scrim to stay opaque near the bottom — which is most of what the gradient is doing.

Solid band. The screenshot stops at a white strip that holds the same copy. Nothing overlaps.
Highest text contrast, and it survives any screenshot, including a light one.
Cost: it gives up 62px of artwork per card and reads as a caption under a picture — the effect you asked for is weaker.

What one viewport costs on SEO: these cards carry about 45 characters of blurb each, against 150 in direction A, and there is no footer link row. The h2 anchor text and the four slugs are intact, which is the part that matters most.
If you want the longer copy back, keep this exact first screen and put a prose block BELOW the fold. Google indexes the rendered DOM whether or not it is above the fold.
